newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 14.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The Loyalist Volunteer Force was on Tuesday being blamed for the murder of a prominent Irish gaelic games personality, Sean Brown, of Bellaghy, County Derry.

- A commitment to cut the top rate of income tax by five percentage points over five years will be the highlight of the election manifesto of Ireland's main opposition party, Fianna Fail, to be unveiled on Friday.
- The Irish government has confirmed its aim of halving unemployment.
- The Presbyterian Church in Dunloy has appealed for an accomodation to allow parades to take place in the town "with dignity."
- Ireland's politicians will be spared further fallout from the Dunnes Payments to Politicians Tribunal until after the June 6 general election.
- A breakaway loyalist paramilitary group is being blamed for the murder of a Catholic father of six.
- Despite sterling's rise, the Irish pound eased back against Continental currencies, losing a quarter pfennig to 2.5749 marks.

- Ireland's Greencore group could be fined up to six million Irish pounds by the European Union on Wednesday for more than ten years of illegal practices by its subsidiary, Irish Sugar, some of which are believed to be on-going.

- The Irish government on Tuesday rejected an attempt by the Pro-Life Campaign to force it to concede a new constitutional referendum on abortion before polling day, after the lobby group warned that it will seek pre-election public pledges from candidates.
